finding: Native submission and validity must synchronize independently of Lit rendering. The same controller and thin native callback bridge can satisfy the targeted text-control cases. The experiment compares synchronization timing, not proof that a mixin is superior to every possible form base.

sourceObservations.detail: updated(ch) calls setFormValue for value changes; reset assigns value; no native disabled/restoration callback or validity mirroring in the inspected file.
Prior complete source comparison: form-associated mixin and synchronous form values.
Prior complete source comparison: specialized base plus validators; general synchronization in willUpdate. This scratch render variant is not Web Awesome itself.
Submission value and restoration state are distinct native inputs.
Validity flags/message and optional shadow descendant focus anchor belong to ElementInternals.

limitations: Text-control prototype only; no checkbox/radio/number/file/composite or managed-form certification.
Explicit invocation tests restoration callback plumbing only, not browser-driven history restoration or autofill.
No submitter, reportValidity focus, external Field labelling, nested radio/RTL, Firefox/WebKit, assistive technology or React checks.
The prototype uses direct property accessors and a simple required-value rule; it is not the finished shared module.
No final choice of controller/base/mixin interface and no new package is approved.
next: Keep immediate form synchronization in the module contract. Resolve the reusable native callback bridge and control-specific mappings with remaining browser/Field/managed-form cases before Phase 5 approval.
